events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea

cases.refreshed: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick (2009). The book is based on Demick's interviews over a seven-year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare and with frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The adult Non-Fiction book group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Medicare: Enrollment, 2027 Updates and Plan Review Tips

cases.refreshed: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) runs from October 15 through December 7 each year. During this time, Medicare beneficiaries can review and make changes to their Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the coming year. Join HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling & Advocacy Program) for a free educational presentation covering Medicare updates taking effect in 2027, Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review strategies, and important factors to consider when evaluating your coverage options. Learn how to compare plan costs, provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and other benefits to determine whether your current plan continues to meet your needs. Following the presentation, HICAP counselors will be available for free one-on-one counseling sessions to answer Medicare questions and help attendees review their coverage options. HICAP counselors are unbiased and are not affiliated with any insurance company. The one-on-one sessions will be on a first-come, first-served basis. HICAP is a program of Sourcewise providing free Medicare counseling to Santa Clara County residents. Who Should Attend? Current Medicare beneficiaries reviewing their coverage for 2027; Individuals approaching Medicare eligibility; Family members and caregivers assisting a Medicare beneficiary. What You Will Learn: Medicare updates taking effect in 2027; How the Annual Enrollment Period works; Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review tips; How to compare costs, coverage, and provider networks; Prescription drug coverage considerations; When it may make sense to change plans; Resources and assistance available through HICAP. What to Bring: A complete list of your prescription medications, including dosage and quantity, for accurate plan comparisons. Your Medicare card (optional, but helpful). HICAP counselors will have laptops available for Medicare plan reviews, but attendees are welcome to bring their own laptop or tablet. Time Required: The time needed to complete a plan comparison varies depending on the number of prescriptions and coverage options being reviewed. Most plan reviews take approximately 30–60 minutes. This program is intended for Santa Clara County residents. Please register if you would like to receive a reminder about the presentation. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org. About Sourcewise: Since 1973, Sourcewise has provided services and support to seniors in Santa Clara County. Sourcewise aims to inform, educate, and prepare all adults within Santa Clara County to better navigate their health and life options.
